formats.key: SafeTx(address to,uint256 value,bytes data,uint8 operation,uint256 safeTxGas,uint256 baseGas,uint256 gasPrice,address gasToken,address refundReceiver,uint256 nonce)
effects: When the threshold of owner signatures is reached, the Safe runs `data` on `to`, as a call or a delegate call depending on `operation`.
With operation 0 (Call), the Safe sends `value` of native currency to `to` along with the call.
With operation 1 (Delegate Call), `to`'s code runs inside the Safe with the Safe's storage and balances. `value` is ignored and no native currency is sent.
When gasPrice > 0, the Safe pays a gas refund of (gas used + baseGas) * gasPrice. It pays in gasToken, or in native currency (capped at tx.gasprice) when gasToken is zero.
The refund goes to refundReceiver, or to tx.origin (the executor) when refundReceiver is zero. It is paid even when the inner call fails, unless safeTxGas and gasPrice are both 0.
safeTxGas caps the gas given to the inner call, so it bounds the refund. When safeTxGas and gasPrice are both 0, the whole transaction reverts if the inner call fails.
The Safe nonce goes up by one, so any other SafeTx signed for the same nonce can no longer run.
formats.shown: The intent is just 'Safe'. Fields show the target, the native value, the operation type, the nested call decoded as a call to `to`, and raw baseGas, gasPrice, gasToken and refundReceiver; safeTxGas and nonce are hidden.

findings.title: SafeTx decodes nested data as a call to `to` and shows Value even when operation is Delegate Call.
findings.evidence: Executor.execute: `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { success := delegatecall(txGas, to, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0) }`. Descriptor field 'Transaction': {"format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to","amountPath":"value","spenderPath":"@.to"}}. When operation is 1, `to`'s code runs in the Safe's context with the Safe's storage and balances, and `value` is never sent. The nested screen still says what a plain call to `to` would do (for example a token transfer from `to`'s own balance), and the 'Value' field still shows an amount that never moves. The 'Operation type' field does show 'Delegate Call', but nothing explains that the decoded nested call does not apply.
findings.fix: Show the nested `data` as a decoded call only when operation is 0. When operation is 1, show a warning label such as 'Delegate call: runs external code in your Safe' and hide 'Value'. Until the spec supports conditional formats, add a 'Delegate call runs code in your Safe' line to the intent or the operation enum label.

findings.title: SafeTx shows the gas refund's parts as raw numbers and addresses; zero meanings are not explained.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `address payable receiver = refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver; if (gasToken == address(0)) { payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice < tx.gasprice ? gasPrice : tx.gasprice); ...} else { payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice); transferToken(gasToken, receiver, payment) }`. Descriptor: `gasPrice` 'Gas price' raw, `gasToken` 'Gas token' raw, `refundReceiver` 'Gas receiver' raw, `baseGas` 'Gas amount' raw. Gas price has no token or decimals. A zero gas token, which means native currency, shows as 0x000…. A zero receiver, which means tx.origin, shows as 0x000…. The 'Gas amount' label hides that baseGas is extra gas added on top of the gas used.
findings.fix: Use format `tokenAmount` for `gasPrice` with `tokenPath: "gasToken"` and `nativeCurrencyAddress` set to the zero address. Use `addressName` for `gasToken` and `refundReceiver`, with `senderAddress`/a label noting that zero means the executor. Rename `baseGas` to 'Extra refund gas'.

findings.title: SafeTx hides safeTxGas, which bounds the gas refund and decides whether a failed inner call reverts.
findings.evidence: Safe.execTransaction: `success = execute(to, value, data, operation, gasPrice == 0 ? (gasleft() - 2500) : safeTxGas);` and `if (!success && safeTxGas == 0 && gasPrice == 0) { revert }`; then `payment = handlePayment(gasUsed, baseGas, gasPrice, gasToken, refundReceiver)`. Descriptor: {"label":"Safe Tx Gas","path":"safeTxGas","visible":"never"}. With safeTxGas set, the inner call can fail while the nonce is still used up and the refund is still paid.
findings.fix: Make `safeTxGas` visible with format `raw` and label 'Max gas for call', at least when gasPrice is not 0.

findings.title: The SafeTx intent 'Safe' names no action; it does not say it runs a transaction from the Safe.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: "intent": "Safe"; no interpolatedIntent. Safe.execTransaction runs an arbitrary call or delegate call from the Safe and can pay a gas refund.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Execute Safe transaction" and add an interpolatedIntent such as "Execute Safe transaction to {to} with {value}".

findings.title: SafeTx has no test case: delegate call, gas refund and zero-address cases are never covered.
findings.evidence: FORMATS.md: 'cases: 0 (no tx)' for the SafeTx format. The operation enum, a non-zero gasPrice with gasToken and refundReceiver, and the nested calldata are not covered by any case.
findings.fix: Add EIP-712 test cases: a Call with an ERC-20 transfer, a Delegate Call (for example to MultiSend), and a SafeTx with gasPrice > 0 and a token refund.

findings.format: SafeTx(address to,uint256 value,bytes data,uint8 operation,uint256 safeTxGas,uint256 baseGas,uint256 gasPrice,address gasToken,address refundReceiver,uint256 nonce)
findings.title: SafeTx decodes nested data as a call to `to` and shows Value even when operation is Delegate Call.
findings.reason: When operation is 1, execTransaction delegatecalls into `to`, so `to`'s code runs against the Safe's own storage and balances and `value` is never sent. The screen still decodes the nested data as an ordinary call to `to` and shows Value as if it moves. The 'Operation type' enum only says 'Delegate Call' and does not correct the nested call's stated outcome. The severity guide lists this exact pattern as critical, and none of the not-critical cases covers it.
findings.quote: Executor.sol execute(): `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { success := delegatecall(txGas, to, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0) }` (here `value` is not passed; only the `call` branch sends `value`), reached from Safe.execTransaction line 180 `execute(to, value, data, operation, ...)`, which does not restrict operation. Descriptor field 'Transaction': {"format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to","amountPath":"value","spenderPath":"@.to"}} is shown unconditionally, with 'Value' as an amount. Severity guide example: "Embedded calldata is decoded as a call to `to` while `operation` can make it a delegate call that runs `to`'s code in the signer's account" is critical.

findings.title: SafeTx decodes nested data as a call to `to` and shows Value even when operation is Delegate Call.
findings.reason: The delegate-call branch executes in the Safe’s context and does not send `value`, but the descriptor unconditionally presents that value as the nested call’s amount. Showing “Delegate Call” does not correct the nested execution context; the severity guide explicitly identifies this mismatch as critical.
